title: Resort Lodging Nightly Tariff and Published Rate Windows
content:
## Published nightly tariff, Resort Lodging

The nightly rate carried by each Resort Lodging unit type is the rate in USD published for it in the window a night falls in. Three rates are published for every unit type: the base nightly rate, which is the rate outside the peak and holiday windows; the peak nightly rate, which is the rate inside the published peak window; and the holiday nightly rate, which is the rate inside the published holiday window.

| Unit type | Base nightly rate (USD) | Peak nightly rate (USD) | Holiday nightly rate (USD) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base Village Inn Room | 189.00 | 269.00 | 369.00 |
| Slopeside Studio | 279.00 | 389.00 | 529.00 |
| Slopeside One-Bedroom Residence | 419.00 | 589.00 | 789.00 |
| Slopeside Two-Bedroom Residence | 629.00 | 869.00 | 1190.00 |
| Mountain Lodge Suite | 749.00 | 1050.00 | 1450.00 |
| Summit Penthouse Residence | 1290.00 | 1790.00 | 2450.00 |
| Private Mountain Chalet | 2450.00 | 3390.00 | 4690.00 |

## The published windows

The holiday window runs from its first date, 2026-12-19, to its last date, 2027-01-02. The peak window runs from its first date, 2027-01-03, to its last date, 2027-03-14. Both windows are published alike for every unit type above.

| Window | First date | Last date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Holiday | 2026-12-19 | 2027-01-02 |
| Peak | 2027-01-03 | 2027-03-14 |

### Reading the windows at their edges (hypothetical dates)

A night of the second of January 2027 is the last date of the holiday window and therefore falls inside it. A night of the third of January 2027 is the first date of the peak window and therefore falls inside the peak window and not the holiday one. A night of the fifteenth of March 2027 falls after the last date of the peak window and so lies outside both published windows.
